title: Theo and the Tide
premise: Silas Winterbourne built a career orchestrating other people's perfect days while quietly answering a decade of letters from a stranger on a remote island — letters signed only 'T.' When Theo, the letter-writer, moves in next door and turns out to be his newest client's estranged heir, Silas must plan the wedding that will disinherit them. As the last ferry of the season approaches, Silas discovers the letters were never anonymous, and Theo knew who he was all along. In the end, Silas walks away from the career that saved him, boards the ferry with Theo, and lets the truth — not loyalty to his own survival — decide what he inherits.
about_author: Beatrix Dunmore is the pen name of a former coastal innkeeper who spent fifteen years watching weddings come and go across a harbour she never left. She writes love stories set where the tide keeps its own schedule.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A jaded wedding planner arrives on Greywater Island to stage a society wedding, dreading the assignment that will make or break his firm. He learns his neighbour in the rented cottage is Theo Marsh, the island's lighthouse keeper's heir — and recognizes the handwriting from ten years of letters he's kept in a shoebox. Emotional beat: stunned recognition masked as polite distance.

chapters.title: Letters in the Shoebox
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Silas and Theo circle each other through shared errands and deliberate silences, each testing what the other knows. Theo admits writing the letters but claims they ended years ago; Silas hides that he answered every one. Meanwhile the bride, Margot Ashcombe, reveals Theo is the disinherited heir her wedding settlement depends on erasing. Emotional beat: intimacy building on a foundation of mutual concealment.

chapters.title: What the Tide Takes
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The rehearsal dinner collapses when Margot demands Silas publicly confirm Theo signed away the inheritance willingly — a lie Theo told to protect someone else. Silas must choose: back the lie and save his career, or tell the truth about the coerced settlement he helped draft. He tells it. Emotional beat: betrayal turning into the first honest thing between them.

chapters.title: Before the Boat Leaves
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Ruined professionally and lighter for it, Silas finds Theo packing to leave before the shame does. At the dock, Silas confesses he wrote back — every letter, every year — and offers the shoebox as proof. Margot, moved by the scandal of honesty, restores Theo's inheritance; Theo offers something better instead. They board together as the tide turns. Emotional beat: surrender, then arrival.
